title: Where the Crawdads Sing
description: A girl raised alone in the North Carolina marshes becomes the suspect in a local man's death. Half courtroom procedural, half natural history, and it sold like almost nothing else that decade.

title: Little Fires Everywhere
description: A planned Ohio suburb, a tenant artist who will not follow its rules, and a custody fight over a Chinese-American baby. Ng is interested in what respectability costs.

title: Everything I Never Told You
description: A mixed-race family in 1970s Ohio after the middle daughter is found in the lake. Opens with the death and works backwards through everyone's silence.

title: A Little Life
description: Four college friends in New York over decades, narrowing onto one man's history of abuse. Long, relentless, and genuinely divisive about whether the suffering is earned.

title: The Goldfinch
description: A boy survives the museum bombing that kills his mother and walks out with a Dutch painting. Dickensian in shape and length, and it won the Pulitzer.

title: A Man Called Ove
description: A widower with rigid views about parking and inferior cars keeps being interrupted in his attempts to die by the family that moved in next door.

title: Anxious People
description: A failed bank robber takes an apartment viewing hostage and the witnesses cannot agree on anything. Comic, then abruptly not.

title: Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine
description: A meticulous, deeply isolated office worker begins, reluctantly, to have a life. The comedy of her literal-mindedness runs directly into what happened to her face.

title: The Midnight Library
description: A woman between life and death browses a library of the lives she might have lived. Schematic on purpose, and it reached an enormous number of people at the right moment.

title: Lessons in Chemistry
description: A chemist pushed out of research in 1960s California ends up presenting a cookery programme and teaching housewives thermodynamics. Angrier than its packaging.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
description: Two friends make video games together for thirty years and never quite manage to be a couple or to stop. Serious about games as a form.

title: Demon Copperhead
description: David Copperfield relocated to the Virginia mountains during the opioid epidemic, narrated by a boy passed between foster placements. Won the Pulitzer.

title: The Poisonwood Bible
description: A Baptist missionary drags his wife and four daughters to the Belgian Congo in 1959. Narrated by the five women, none of whom forgive him.

title: The Kite Runner
description: A Kabul boyhood, a betrayal in an alley, and a return decades later under the Taliban. The book that put Afghanistan on Western book club tables.

title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
description: Two women married to the same man in Kabul across three decades of war. Harder than The Kite Runner and better constructed.

title: Life of Pi
description: A boy adrift in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger for 227 days, and then a second account of the same voyage. The ending asks which story you prefer.

title: The Help
description: Black maids in 1960s Jackson, Mississippi tell their stories to a young white writer. Hugely popular and heavily criticised for centring the white author-figure.

title: The Secret Life of Bees
description: A white girl in 1964 South Carolina runs away with her Black housekeeper and is taken in by three beekeeping sisters. Sweet-natured about a violent year.

title: The Immortalists
description: Four siblings are told the dates of their deaths by a fortune teller in 1969 and live the next fifty years accordingly. One life per section.

title: Commonwealth
description: A kiss at a christening breaks two marriages and mixes six children. Fifty years of the consequences, told out of order.

title: Bel Canto
description: Terrorists take a diplomatic party hostage in South America and the siege lasts months, during which everyone becomes attached to a visiting soprano.

title: The Dutch House
description: A brother and sister sit in a parked car outside the house they were expelled from, for decades. A fairy tale about a stepmother, told realistically.

title: Pachinko
description: Four generations of a Korean family in Japan, where they remain foreigners regardless of how long they stay. Opens in 1910 and does not stop for eighty years.

title: Homegoing
description: Two half-sisters in eighteenth-century Ghana, one married to a slaver and one sold. Then a chapter per descendant, alternating across three hundred years.

title: The Vanishing Half
description: Twin sisters from a Louisiana town of light-skinned Black families run away at sixteen; one returns and one passes as white for the rest of her life.

title: An American Marriage
description: A year into a marriage, the husband is wrongly convicted and sentenced to twelve years. Told partly in letters, and it refuses to make the wife's waiting simple.

title: Such a Fun Age
description: A Black babysitter is accused of kidnapping in a supermarket, and her white employer decides to make it right. Excruciatingly precise about good intentions.

title: Americanah
description: A Nigerian woman blogs about American race from the outside while her first love builds a life in London. Adichie on hair, class and what emigration does to a couple.

title: The Sympathizer
description: A communist double agent embedded with South Vietnamese officers in Los Angeles writes a confession. Furious, funny, and won the Pulitzer.

title: There There
description: Twelve Native characters converging on a powwow in Oakland. Urban rather than reservation, which is the point Orange opens the book by making.

title: The Overstory
description: Nine strangers drawn into the defence of the last old-growth forests. Structured like a tree, and it changed how a lot of readers look at one.

title: Sea of Tranquility
description: 1912 Vancouver Island, a 2203 moon colony, and a novelist on tour during a plague. A time-travel investigation that keeps returning to the same few seconds in a forest.

title: The Glass Hotel
description: A Ponzi scheme, a remote hotel in British Columbia, and a woman who disappears from a container ship. Mandel writes money as haunting.

title: Cloud Cuckoo Land
description: A lost Greek manuscript links the siege of Constantinople, an Idaho library, and a generation ship. Doerr on books as the thing that survives.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
description: A blind French girl and a German boy conscripted for his talent with radios, converging on Saint-Malo in 1944. Short chapters, and it won the Pulitzer.

title: The Tattooist of Auschwitz
description: A Slovakian Jew assigned to tattoo numbers on arrivals falls in love with a woman in the queue. Based on interviews, and historians have disputed a good deal of it.

title: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
description: A dead war photographer has seven moons to solve his own murder in 1990 Colombo. Won the Booker; the afterlife has queues and bureaucracy.

title: Shuggie Bain
description: A boy in 1980s Glasgow looking after his alcoholic mother while everyone else leaves. Won the Booker, and it is as hard as that summary sounds.

title: Hamnet
description: The death of Shakespeare's eleven-year-old son, told from his wife's side and barely mentioning the playwright by name. The plague chapter is extraordinary.

title: Klara and the Sun
description: A solar-powered artificial friend in a shop window is bought for a sick girl. Narrated by Klara, whose understanding of what she sees is partial and touching.

title: Lincoln in the Bardo
description: Willie Lincoln's night in a Georgetown crypt, narrated by the dead and by fragments of real historical sources. Won the Booker; formally unlike anything else.

title: The Nickel Boys
description: A boy bound for college is sent instead to a Florida reform school modelled on the real Dozier School. Spare, and the structure withholds one thing.

title: The Underground Railroad
description: The railroad rendered as a literal train under the ground, and each state a different experiment in American racism. Won the Pulitzer.

title: If We Were Villains
description: Seven Shakespeare students at an elite conservatory, one body, and a narrator telling it ten years later from prison. Dark academia, openly in Tartt's debt.

title: Rules of Civility
description: A typist's year in 1938 Manhattan after a chance meeting in a jazz bar on New Year's Eve. Towles on the American self-invention machine.

title: The Lincoln Highway
description: Four boys in 1954 set out from Nebraska for California and go east instead. Ten days, several narrators, and a mounting sense of a mistake.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
description: Four residents of a retirement village who meet weekly over cold cases get a live one. Funny, and clear-eyed about being old and underestimated.

title: The Man Who Died Twice
description: Elizabeth's first husband turns up having stolen twenty million in diamonds from the wrong people. The second Thursday Murder Club, with a higher body count.

title: The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency
description: Precious Ramotswe sells her father's cattle to open Botswana's first female detective agency. The cases are small and the book is about the country.

title: Still Life
description: Chief Inspector Gamache investigates an archery death in a Quebec village that is not on any map. The village is the reason the series has eighteen more.

title: Magpie Murders
description: An editor reads a golden-age detective novel with the last chapter missing, then has to solve her author's death to find it. Two mysteries, nested.

title: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
description: The same day at a country house repeats, with the investigator waking in a different guest's body each time. A locked-room mystery crossed with a logic problem.

title: The House of the Spirits
description: Three generations of the Trueba family through a century of Chilean politics, ending in the coup. Ghosts and clairvoyance sit beside torture without apology.

title: The Shadow of the Wind
description: A boy in postwar Barcelona chooses a book from the Cemetery of Forgotten Books and finds someone has been burning every other copy.

title: The Elegance of the Hedgehog
description: A concierge hiding her erudition and a twelve-year-old planning suicide, in the same Paris building. Both change when a Japanese tenant moves in.

title: My Brilliant Friend
description: Two girls in a poor Naples neighbourhood in the 1950s, one of whom is allowed to keep going to school. The first of four, and the friendship is not sentimental.

title: The Days of Abandonment
description: A woman comes apart over a Turin summer after her husband leaves. Short and much more violent in feeling than the Neapolitan novels.

title: Convenience Store Woman
description: A woman who has worked the same Tokyo convenience store for eighteen years and is perfectly content is pressured into a life she is supposed to want.

title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
description: A Tokyo café where one seat sends you back in time, on strict conditions, and nothing you do can change the present. Four linked stories about saying the thing anyway.

title: The Housekeeper and the Professor
description: A mathematician whose memory lasts eighty minutes, his housekeeper, and her son. They communicate mostly in number theory, which is more moving than it sounds.

title: Norwegian Wood
description: A student in late-sixties Tokyo between the withdrawn girlfriend of his dead best friend and someone entirely alive. Murakami's most straightforwardly realist novel.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
description: A man looking for his wife's cat, then his wife, descends a dry well and into Japan's occupation of Manchuria. Enormous and deliberately unresolved.

title: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
description: A hijra who moves into a Delhi graveyard, and a woman connected to the Kashmir insurgency. Roy's second novel, twenty years after the first, and much angrier.

title: A Suitable Boy
description: A mother's search for a husband for her daughter in newly independent India, across 1,300 pages of four families and a general election.

title: White Teeth
description: Two wartime friends and their families in north London over fifty years. Smith was twenty-four, and the book is as loud and crowded as the city it describes.

title: On Beauty
description: Two feuding academic families in a New England college town. Howards End restaged around affirmative action and a Rembrandt argument.

title: Brooklyn
description: A young woman sent from Enniscorthy to 1950s Brooklyn builds a life, then is called home. Very quiet, and the last fifty pages are agonising.

title: Oryx and Crake
description: The last man alive remembers the friend who engineered the plague and the corporate compounds they grew up in. Atwood's other dystopia, and the more prescient one.

title: The Testaments
description: Gilead fifteen years on, told by three women including Aunt Lydia. Written after the television series and much more interested in how a regime rots from inside.

title: The Power
description: Teenage girls develop the ability to deliver electric shocks and the world's power balance inverts within a decade. Framed as a historical novel written far in the future.

title: Severance
description: A New York publishing drone keeps going to the office through a fever that leaves its victims repeating routines until they die. Satire of work, written before 2020.

title: Blood Meridian
description: A boy rides with a scalp-hunting gang across the 1850s borderlands, alongside Judge Holden. Frequently called the great American novel and almost unreadably violent.

title: No Country for Old Men
description: A welder takes two million dollars from a drug deal in the desert and is hunted by a man with a cattle gun. Stripped to dialogue and consequence.

title: Lonesome Dove
description: Two retired Texas Rangers drive cattle from the Rio Grande to Montana. Won the Pulitzer, and it is the book that made the western respectable again.

title: The Son
description: Three generations of a Texas dynasty from Comanche captivity to oil. Told in rotation, and each generation's wealth rests on the previous one's atrocity.

title: East of Eden
description: Two families in the Salinas Valley replaying Cain and Abel across generations. Steinbeck thought it his best; the word timshel does a lot of the work.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
description: The Joads driven from Oklahoma to California by dust and the banks. Burned publicly on publication, won the Pulitzer, and remains hard to argue with.

title: Of Mice and Men
description: Two migrant workers with a plan for a small farm, and a man who does not know his own strength. A hundred pages, and the ending is visible from the first.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
description: A lawyer defends a Black man against a rape charge in 1930s Alabama, narrated by his young daughter. The most assigned novel in American schools, for better and worse.

title: The Great Gatsby
description: A bootlegger throws parties across the bay from the woman he reorganised his life around. Short, and almost every sentence is doing something.

title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
description: Janie Crawford's three marriages, told to a friend on a porch. Dismissed on publication, recovered decades later, and the dialect is the achievement.

title: The Color Purple
description: Letters from a Black woman in rural Georgia, first to God and then to her sister. Won the Pulitzer and is still routinely banned.

title: Song of Solomon
description: A man called Milkman traces his family south and finds a story about flight. Morrison's third novel and the one that made her reputation.

title: Sula
description: Two girls in an Ohio hill town, one who leaves and one who stays, and the betrayal between them. Under two hundred pages and it holds a whole community.

title: A Visit from the Goon Squad
description: Thirteen linked chapters around a record executive and his assistant, jumping decades and voices, including one told entirely in PowerPoint. Won the Pulitzer.

title: The Corrections
description: A mother wants her three adult children home for one last Christmas while her husband's Parkinson's advances. Franzen on the Midwest and the market, at length.

title: Freedom
description: A liberal St Paul couple, their best friend the rock musician, and a mountaintop-removal conservation deal. Suburban decency examined until it cracks.

title: Middlesex
description: Three generations of a Greek-American family in Detroit, narrated by an intersex man tracing a recessive gene from a village on Mount Olympus. Won the Pulitzer.

title: The Virgin Suicides
description: Five sisters in 1970s Michigan, remembered decades later by the neighbourhood boys who watched them and understood nothing. Narrated in the collective we.

title: Olive Kitteridge
description: Thirteen stories in a coastal Maine town, all touching a retired maths teacher who is difficult in ways the book never smooths over. Won the Pulitzer.

title: My Name Is Lucy Barton
description: A woman in a New York hospital is visited by the mother she has not spoken to in years. Five days of talk that avoids everything important.

title: Gilead
description: A dying Iowa preacher writes a long letter to the young son who will not remember him. Won the Pulitzer, and it is almost entirely interior.

title: Housekeeping
description: Two orphaned sisters raised by a drifting aunt in an Idaho lake town. Robinson's first novel and its sentences are the reason people talk about it.

title: Stoner
description: The unremarkable life of a Missouri farm boy who becomes an English professor. Ignored on publication, rediscovered fifty years later, and quietly devastating.
